land.text: the Kingdom of France in its 1791 borders, whose monarchy the Convention abolished on 21 September 1792

predecessors.note: 'The Republic was founded on 21 September 1792 during the French Revolution'; Cliopatria's Kingdom of France row ends in 1791 and its 1791 shape includes the colonies.

land.text: the whole republic, Belgium and the Rhineland included, passes to the Directory

successors.note: 'On 3 November 1795, the Directory was established.' The republic as a state continues to 1804 on the Wikipedia page; Cliopatria and this project cut it into Convention (this dossier), Directory (french-directory) and Consulate (french-consulate), all in colour family 'france'.

correction.text: 'The Duchy of Savoy (1792)' and 'The County of Nice (1793)': the Cliopatria shape plus Savoy from 1792 and the Nice country from 1793 (the ledger dates each)

keyframe_review.note: 571,208 km2 for 1792-1793, colonies included (Cliopatria's modern-country list shows Senegal and Mauritius). The shape holds no Savoy and no Nice: the dated list of the page gives 'The Duchy of Savoy (1792)' and 'The County of Nice (1793)', so the correction adds both; Montbeliard (annexed in 1793) is a speck inside the cell grid and is carried by the ledger. Infobox: 3,000,000 km2 'including colonies' in 1800 (Louisiana was French 1800-1803), which is 5 times this shape and not comparable: the shape is the metropole plus some colonies, and stands. Avignon and the Comtat Venaissin (1791) are already inside.

644,860 km2 for 1794-1795. The shape holds Savoy, Nice, Belgium with Liege, the left bank of the Rhine and Maastricht, which the dated list of the page makes French as 'The Austrian Netherlands and the Prince-Bishopric of Liege (1795)', 'The German states on the left bank of the Rhine (1797)'; the page and Cliopatria differ by a year or more because Cliopatria draws the conquest of 1794 (Fleurus, 26 June) where the page dates the legal annexation, so the ledger keeps the lands as occupied until the annexation. Corsica is correctly absent: the Anglo-Corsican Kingdom was 'Established: 15-19 June 1794'. Infobox 3.0 M km2 (1800, with colonies) is not comparable.

ledger.note: 1792: the Republic annexes Savoy. The page's dated list reads 'The Duchy of Savoy (1792)'; the war page adds that the French were 'occupying the Duchy of Savoy and the County of Nice'. The page gives no month; Savoy was part of the Kingdom of Sardinia.

region.text: Speyer, Worms and Mainz along the Rhine, captured in the 1792 campaign

ledger.note: Autumn 1792: the French campaign on the Rhine. The page: the French were 'capturing Speyer, Worms and Mainz along the Rhine' in the 1792 campaign (no month given).

region.text: France in the borders of 1791, the departments of the kingdom, with Paris as the capital

ledger.note: 21 September 1792: the National Convention abolishes the monarchy and France becomes a republic. 'The Republic was founded on 21 September 1792'; infobox 'Abolition of the French monarchy: 21 September 1792'; capital Paris. The page names France, not a frontier.

region.text: the Austrian Netherlands, occupied after Jemappes (6 November 1792)

ledger.note: November 1792: French victory at Jemappes opens the war for the Austrian Netherlands. The page: 'winning a great victory over the Austrians at Jemappes on 6 November 1792', after which 'the Netherlands were then occupied'. The page does not mention the Austrian return of 1793, so the zone stays contested until Fleurus.
1793: the Republic annexes the County of Nice. The page's dated list reads 'The County of Nice (1793)'; no month on the page.

region.text: County of Montbéliard, held by the House of Württemberg, 'annexed in 1793'

ledger.note: 1793: the Republic annexes the County of Montbeliard. The page: 'annexed in 1793', a possession of the House of Wurttemberg; the page gives no month (the duchy-of-wurttemberg dossier has November).

region.text: the Prince-Bishopric of Liège, taken in the 1794 campaign

ledger.note: 1794: French armies hold the Prince-Bishopric of Liege, drawn French by Cliopatria from 1794. The page lists only the legal act, 'The Austrian Netherlands and the Prince-Bishopric of Liege (1795)'; the 1794 start is bridged from the Cliopatria shape and Fleurus.

1794: the fighting for the Rhineland ends in a French hold. The page: Fleurus 'gained all of the Austrian Netherlands and the Rhineland for France'; the Peace of Basel (1795) 'recognized France's occupation of the left bank of the Rhine'.

region.text: the Rhineland / the left bank of the Rhine, held by French armies after Fleurus

ledger.note: 1794: French armies hold the left bank of the Rhine. The page: 'Battle of Fleurus (1794) gained all of the Austrian Netherlands and the Rhineland for France'; the Peace of Basel then 'recognized France's occupation of the left bank of the Rhine'. The Directory annexes it in 1797. [Reviewer eu-20-a, 2026-10-31: region narrowed to the left bank: the gazetteer's Rhineland is Rheinland-Pfalz + Saarland + all of Nordrhein-Westfalen, right bank included; intersected with Cliopatria's 1794 shape, which stops at the Rhine.]

region.text: Corsica, the Anglo-Corsican Kingdom established 15-19 June 1794

ledger.note: June 1794: Corsica leaves the Republic for the British crown. The Anglo-Corsican Kingdom page: 'Established: 15-19 June 1794', a consulta at Corte in 1793, and the 'Siege of Calvi: 17 June - 10 August 1794'; capital Corte until 1795, Bastia from 1795. The island returns to the Directory in October 1796.

region.text: the Low Countries the Austrians gave up contesting after Fleurus (26 June 1794)

ledger.note: 26 June 1794: Fleurus ends the Austrian fight for the Low Countries. 'The Austrians gave up on contesting the Low Countries after the Battle of Fleurus (26 June)'; the territory was 'overrun by the French in 1794'. The war page adds that Fleurus 'gained all of the Austrian Netherlands and the Rhineland for France'.

region.text: the Austrian Netherlands overrun after Fleurus, not yet annexed

ledger.note: 26 June 1794: France holds the Austrian Netherlands but has not annexed them. The page: 'overrun by the French in 1794' after Fleurus, and 'On 1 October 1795 the departments were activated and the definitive annexation started'. Drawn hatched until then.
1795: Liege is annexed with Belgium. The page lists 'The Austrian Netherlands and the Prince-Bishopric of Liege (1795)'; the month is not given.
1795: the Prince-Bishopric of Liege is annexed. The page lists it with the Austrian Netherlands under '(1795)'; no month given.

region.text: the Netherlands of the Batavian Republic, proclaimed 19 January 1795

ledger.note: 19 January 1795: the Batavian Republic is proclaimed as France's sister republic. 'It was proclaimed on 19 January 1795 after the Batavian Revolution'; status 'Sister republic of the French First Republic and First French Empire'; 'intervention by the French Republic led to the downfall of the old Dutch Republic'. A client state, drawn in the lighter tint.

16 May 1795: the Treaty of The Hague gives France Maastricht, Venlo and Zeelandic Flanders. The Batavian Republic 'ceded to France the territories of Maastricht, Venlo, and Zeelandic Flanders'; the treaty 'was signed on May 16, 1795'. Cliopatria draws Maastricht French from 1794.

region.text: the Austrian Netherlands become French departments

ledger.note: 1 October 1795: Belgium is annexed. 'On 1 October 1795 the departments were activated and the definitive annexation started'; Austria 'relinquished its claim' by the Treaty of Campo Formio (17 October 1797).

1 October 1795: the Austrian Netherlands become French departments. 'On 1 October 1795 the departments were activated and the definitive annexation started'; the territorial-evolution page lists 'The Austrian Netherlands and the Prince-Bishopric of Liege (1795)'.

region.text: the republic of the Convention, Belgium and the left bank of the Rhine included

ledger.note: 3 November 1795: the Directory replaces the Convention. 'On 3 November 1795, the Directory was established.' The page treats the Republic as one state to 18 May 1804; this project ends the Convention's dossier here and continues in french-directory.

wars.name: War of the First Coalition

zones.text: the Austrian Netherlands, Jemappes 6 November 1792, Fleurus 1794
Speyer, Worms and Mainz 1792; the left bank
the Duchy of Savoy and the County of Nice, occupied

wars.outcome: '20 April 1792 - 17 October 1797'. France wins: Fleurus 'gained all of the Austrian Netherlands and the Rhineland for France'; the Treaty of Basel (1795) took Prussia out and 'a treaty of peace between France and Spain followed in July'; Austria ceded Belgium and recognised French control of the Rhineland in October 1797.
wars.note: The page gives Prussia's Basel treaty twice, '17 May 1795' and '5 April 1795'. Sardinia was forced to peace by the Treaty of Paris (1796), recorded in french-directory.

wars.name: British intervention in Corsica

zones.text: the island, held by the Anglo-Corsican Kingdom

wars.outcome: The Anglo-Corsican Kingdom was 'Established: 15-19 June 1794' after the 'Siege of Calvi: 17 June - 10 August 1794'; the British evacuated on 11 October 1796 and France retook Bastia on 19 October 1796.

certainty.note: The departments of the kingdom, Savoy and Nice are fixed administrative lines. The occupied Low Countries and left bank of the Rhine are fighting fronts until the annexations of 1795 and 1797, and the colonies in Cliopatria's shape are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria row 'French First Republic' 1792..1795 (two shapes) reviewed; the Directory (1796-1799) and Consulate (1800-1804) are separate rows and dossiers although the Wikipedia page treats them as phases of one republic that ends on 18 May 1804. Pages: the French First Republic page gives no territory at all (it only lists Louisiana 1800-1803), so annexations come from 'Territorial evolution of France', which has years but no months; months for Belgium (1 October 1795) and Fleurus (26 June 1794) come from the Austrian Netherlands page. Not covered because no page was opened within the 1-2 page budget (the budget was exceeded by five pages shared with french-directory and batavian-republic): the War in the Vendee and the federalist revolts of 1793 (rebel-held land; no Cliopatria row; needs a rebel dossier), the Anglo-Piedmontese front at the Massif de l'Authion, Toulon 1793, Saint-Domingue and the colonies drawn in Cliopatria's shapes, Mulhouse and Geneva (1798, Directory), the Mainz Republic (1793). Gazetteer names needed: place 'Montbéliard', place 'Venlo', region 'Zeelandic Flanders' (Zeeuws-Vlaanderen). Counterpart dossiers that exist and agree: habsburg-netherlands (occupation 26 June 1794, annexation 1 October 1795), prince-bishopric-of-liege (annexation 1795), anglo-corsican-kingdom, duchy-of-wurttemberg (Montbeliard). The Batavian vassal_start and the Rhineland occupation_start have no end here because both continue under french-directory (restarted there on 26 October 1795; the Rhineland occupation ends with Campo Formio, 17 October 1797). The 1792 shape lacks Savoy/Nice and the 1794 shape draws the 1794 conquests as plain territory; the hatched occupation in the ledger is what the map should show.
